{{distinguish|Monad (category theory)}}
In [[homological algebra]], a '''monad''' is a 3-term [[chain complex|complex]]

: ''A'' → ''B'' → ''C''

of objects in some [[abelian category]] whose middle term ''B'' is [[Projective object|projective]], whose first map ''A''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''B'' is [[injective function|injective]], and whose second map ''B''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''C'' is [[surjective function|surjective]]. Equivalently, a monad is a projective object together with a 3-step [[Filtration (mathematics)|filtration]] ''B'' ⊃ ker(''B''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''C'') ⊃ im(''A''&nbsp;→&nbsp;''B''). In practice ''A'', ''B'', and ''C'' are often [[vector bundle]]s over some space, and there are several minor extra conditions that some authors add to the definition. Monads were introduced by Horrocks.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Horrocks |first=G. |date=October 1964 |title=Vector Bundles on the Punctured Spectrum of a Local Ring |url=http://doi.wiley.com/10.1112/plms/s3-14.4.689 |journal=Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society |language=en |volume=s3-14 |issue=4 |pages=689–713 |doi=10.1112/plms/s3-14.4.689|url-access=subscription }}</ref>
